title: Antinomie job and query API, version 1
description: Generated from the Rust types of the antinomie-service crate. Do not edit.

name.description: File name hint, 1 to 128 bytes, no `/`, no NUL.

priority.description: 0 to 9, higher starts first; default 5; the policy sets a ceiling.

labels.description: At most 16 pairs; key 1 to 32 bytes `[a-z0-9._-]`, value up to 128 bytes.

JobSpec.description:
What a caller submits with `job.submit`, and the resolved form a [`Job`]
carries (policy defaults filled in; `sample.path` removed for remote
callers; `sample.sha256` always set after prechecks).

[`Job`]: super::job::Job

sha256.description: A sample already in the library.

path.description:
Local-only: a regular file on the host, read once and archived into
the library. Never present in a remote reply.

upload_id.description: A finished staged upload (sealed, hashed); expires after 24 hours unused.

SampleSource.description: The sample of a job. Exactly one member is set ([`SampleSource::validate`]).

Sha256Hex.description: A sample's identity: the lowercase SHA-256.

UploadId.description: The identifier of a staged upload.

timeout_s.description:
Wall-clock limit of the run in seconds, 5 to the policy `max_run_s`
(default policy 300, maximum 1800). Reaching it ends the run normally
(`end_reason: time_limit`); it is not a failure.

args.description: Program arguments, at most 64, each at most 4096 bytes.

network_capture.description: Packet capture for the run; default true on a VM with a network card.

memory_dump.description: VM memory after the run's tree ends.

report_defang.description: Defang indicators in HTML, PDF and Markdown; default true (B-W10).

keep_on_failure.description:
Leave the VM and its disk as they are when the job fails (needs policy
permission); the lane is then quarantined with reason
`kept_for_inspection`.

Overrides.description:
The per-job overrides of the policy (design 5.4.1). `overrides.base` and
`overrides.stealth` of revision 1 are removed: the lane VM fixes both.

RunAs.description:
A guest identity: `user` (UID/GID 1000, the default), `root` (needs policy
permission) or explicit ids.

RunIn.description:
How the program is run in the guest. v1 supports `app_terminal` only
(decided B-H24); the other two are reserved and fail `unsupported`.

Route.description:
A network route by the engine's own serde spelling (`RouteKind`). v1 jobs
accept only `drop` and `inet_sim`; the others are valid spellings that fail
`unsupported` with `details.reason = "live_route_not_in_v1"`.

CoreDump.description: A process core on exit: a switch, or its limits.

StaticChecks.description:
Host-side static analysis of the library copy, run in the `analyse` stage:
`none`, `triage` (the engine's eleven-tool set) or a list of checks.

StaticCheck.description: The names of `AnalysisKind` in lower snake case (`analysis/types.rs:7`).

DetectionSelection.description: Which detection engines run on the evidence.

waiting_for.description: While `queued`: why it is not running yet; null otherwise.

failure.description:
Set when `failed` or `rejected`. Null for `partial`: a partial job
explains itself only through `warnings`.

Job.description: The job object returned by `job.get`, `job.submit` and the list.

JobState.description: The job states of design 5.6. `state` and `outcome` are equal once terminal.

WaitingFor.description: Why a `queued` job is not running yet.

Outcome.description: A terminal state: the set `outcome` takes.

JobSample.description: The library sample of a job, once archived.

PolicyRef.description: The frozen policy: its name and the digest of the exact content used.

JobVm.description: The VM a job ran on.

Revert.description: How the lane VM was made clean (design 4.5).

exit.description: The exit code when the program exited.

signal.description: The signal number when it was killed by one.

directory.description: Local-only; absent from every remote reply.

JobRecording.description:
The recording of the job's run. `run_key` is the address of every
`recording.*` read.

label.description: Null only when the policy explicitly disables the mapping.

score.description: 0 to 100 from the policy formula; null when no rule sets one.

ioc_dataset_count.description:
Loaded indicator datasets. With zero, indicators cannot produce
`malicious` and `basis` says so.

AssessmentKind.description:
`report::Summary.assessment`, or `inconclusive` when the run or triage did
not complete.

Tier.description: A finding or detection tier; `none` for no finding.

KeyBehaviour.description: One of at most 25 key behaviours.

DetectionHit.description: A hit of a detection engine (YARA, IDS, Sigma).

raw_indicators.description:
The artifact keeps indicators raw (JSON, MISP, STIX, or an HTML, PDF or
Markdown report exported without defang). Needs `read`; clients must not
render it as active content.

ArtifactId.description: The identifier of a job artifact.

Warning.description:
A non-fatal note. Capped at 1000 entries; the 1001st is replaced by one
`warnings_truncated` entry.

detail.description:
The engine's own error text, truncated to 2 KiB, host paths removed for
remote callers.

waiting_for.description: While `queued`: why it is not running yet; null otherwise.

failure.description:
Set when `failed` or `rejected`. Null for `partial`: a partial job
explains itself only through `warnings`.

Submitted.description:
The result of `job.submit`: the stored job, plus `replayed` when an
idempotency key returned the original.

ts_ms.description: The time the service recorded it.

oneOf.description: Accepted by `job.submit`.
Any change of state, stage or `waiting_for`.
Per stage.
Ephemeral: not stored, no `seq`. At most 4 per second per job.
The program started.
An artifact became available.
Triage finished.

Event.description:
The envelope. `seq` counts within one job (job scope) or one service epoch
(engine scope) from 1; `gseq` is strictly increasing across the service,
persisted and never reused. Both are absent on ephemeral events.

MetricsVm.description:
Vm figures of `job.metrics`; numbers only. `cpu_percent` is the host QEMU
process figure; the guest figures come from `VmResources.guest`.

oneOf.description: A subscription with no event for 15 seconds.

Frame.description:
`engine.hello` and `engine.ping`: neither is an event (no `seq`, no
`gseq`, never stored). The wire form is
`{"frame": "engine.hello", "data": {...}}`.

epoch.description: A random id per daemon start.

truncated.description:
True when the requested resume point is older than the retained
events; the client must re-synchronise with `job.list`.

Hello.description: The one hello shape (socket connection and `events.subscribe`).

oneOf.description: A separate service process.
The service runs inside the web process.

field.description: The offending request field, when one is to blame.

ApiError.description: The error of a failed operation.

ErrorCode.description:
The error codes. `unauthenticated` and `forbidden` are added by the HTTP
layer only.

custody_ok.description: The cached chain check; null when not checked.

oneOf.description: The `run/PAUSE` file.

DiskLayer.description: Whether the lane VM has a pending run layer (5.12.2).

lanes.description: Concurrent VMs (1 in the first release).

max_sample_bytes.description: The minimum of 5.4.1 for the current lane.

routes.description:
Routes a caller may request under its policies (v1: a subset of
`drop` and `inet_sim`).

static_checks.description: Available check names, tool presence considered.

accelerator.description: A `tcg` service says so because runs are slow.

IocDataset.description: A loaded indicator dataset and its entry count.

sortable.description:
Empty: the list has a fixed order and a `sort` on it is
`invalid_argument`.

tables.description: For operations with a `tab`: one table per tab value.

OpClass.description:
`C` needs only the engine; `T` needs the Triage scan and can answer
`building`.

oneOf.description: The analysis operations: a run's analysis, or a job's host-side one.
Custody, instead of a run.
The `q` language.
A Wireshark display filter.

FieldType.description: The type of a table column.

FieldInfo.description: A column of a table, copied from the engine's `FieldSpec` lists.

QueryLimits.description: The row, byte and concurrency limits of 5.12.5 and 5.12.6.

EngineHealth.description: The engine counters of `health` (numbers and enums only).

ReadGaps.description: `Snapshot.health.read_gaps` reduced to numbers a client can chart.

PolicySummary.description: A policy a caller may use (`policy.list`); never secrets.

VmSummary.description: A VM a policy can use (`vm.list`); lane VMs carry `lane`.

head.description: The head hash of the verified chain, when one sample was asked for.

Request.description: The request line of the local socket.

Reply.description:
A reply line: `{"id": 7, "ok": true, "result": {...}}`,
`{"id": 7, "ok": false, "error": {...}}`, an event line
`{"id": 7, "event": {...}}`, or a frame line (the hello that starts an
`events.subscribe` answer carries the request `id` beside `frame` and
`data`).

oneOf.description: A subscription with no event for 15 seconds.

policies.description: Glob patterns of the policies the caller may use.

Caller.description:
Who is asking. The CLI uses the OS user (`local:<uid>`), the web layer
fills it from authentication (`web:<user_id>`). The service never trusts a
client-supplied value.

max_chunk.description: The longest chunk one `upload.put` may carry.

data.description: Base64, at most 1 MiB per call on the socket.

with_recording.description: Also remove the recording (the sample is never removed).

ByteRange.description: A byte range of an artifact.

tag.description: One tag as `KIND=VALUE` (a bare value is a custom tag).

tags.description: More tags a sample must also have (additive to the 5.3 table).

all.description: Include samples whose archive was removed (additive).

SampleGetParams.description:
`sample.get`: the sample, and on request the routes that brought it in, its
custody events and its runs (additive members of the 5.3 table).

SampleDownloadParams.description:
`sample.download`: a range of the library archive (an AES zip), at most
1 MiB per call, as Base64.

Op.description: The stable operation name used on the local socket (`op`) and in the CLI.

oneOf.description: `conflict`: the recording grew or the filter changed.
`precondition_failed`: earlier file bytes while the layer is pending.

`precondition_failed`: a Triage read of a recording still being written;
`details.phase` says which phase.
`quota_exceeded`: too many heavy reads; `details.retry_after_s`.
`unavailable`: a read passed its deadline and was cancelled.
`unsupported`: `internet`, `tor`, `vpn` or `socks5` in a v1 job.
`unsupported`: a desktop run mode in a v1 job.
`unsupported`: the core needs a newer guest revision.
`not_found`: the run never produced that data.
`internal`: the Triage scan failed; the next call may start it again.
`internal`: the recording is corrupt or its index cannot be built.

`quota_exceeded`: the connection has 16 requests in flight (or the
socket 256) (local socket, 5.9).

`quota_exceeded`: requests come faster than the socket's rate;
`details.retry_after_s`.
`unavailable`: the socket serves 64 connections already.
`quota_exceeded`: 64 subscriptions of this client or 256 in all (A18).
`unavailable`: the daemon is stopping; queued jobs stay queued.

`unavailable`: a request was cancelled by `{"op": "cancel"}` or by the
connection closing.

ErrorReason.description: The values of `details.reason` the contract names (5.7, 5.12.1, 5.12.8).

Sort.description:
A `sort` request: ties keep the default order. Only the fields
`capabilities.queries` names for the operation are allowed.

FileContentParams.description: `recording.files.content`: at most 1 MiB per call. Sensitive.

NetworkPacketsParams.description:
`recording.network.packets`: frame order; `filter` is a Wireshark
display filter, at most 500 rows per page.

AnalysisListParams.description:
`recording.analysis.list`: exactly one of `run_key` (the analysis linked
to a run) or `job_id` (the host-side analysis of a job).

CustodyListParams.description:
`recording.custody.list`: `sha256` instead of `run_key`, or the run's
sample when `run_key` is given.

TerminalReplayParams.description:
`recording.terminal.replay`: at most 256 records; the cursor is a
journal byte offset.

ArtifactGetParams2.description:
`recording.artifact.get`: at most 1 MiB per call; a capture, memory
dump, core or file copy is sensitive.
